# Backseat

> Graph-based workflows for coding agents: structure and direction for a coding agent, enforced. A workflow is a graph: states, the transitions between them, and the instructions for each. The agent a person already uses drives it from its own shell: it reaches a state and is told what to do there and which transitions are open, and anything else is refused with a reason. A long prompt describes the steps; this holds the agent to them.

A workflow is an XState machine with three keys added (`instructions`, `data`, `schema`), written in TypeScript. A person, or their coding agent, writes the machine; an agent drives it through one command-line tool, `node cli.ts --drive`, which teaches itself as it goes. The driving agent needs no brief.

Where a framework like LangGraph drives inference calls, Backseat drives a conversation: the agent runs one command, reads what the workflow says, does the work with its own tools, and asks again. What the workflow knows is kept in its ledger (`context` in the code), and a state's `data` is the part of it the agent is shown. What is enforced is the path: the workflow cannot stop an agent from walking away, and it never advances on anything but a transition it offered, sent with a payload that passed.

## Start

- `npx skills add pottedmeat/backseat-ai --skill backseat-ai` installs the companion skill for writing, reviewing and debugging machines. It routes to the docs installed at `node_modules/backseat-ai/docs/`. With it installed, a coding agent can be asked to build a new workflow, or to turn a workflow written in prose into a machine; it should interview the person first about the steps, what has to be true before moving from each to the next, and what a finished run produces.
- `npx backseat-ai init` sets the working directory up as a project (package.json, tsconfig.json, cli.ts and a catalog) and, with no machine to find, offers a starter. It is safe to run again.
- To run a workflow, the agent runs `node cli.ts --drive create <machine>` and follows what it prints.

## Commands

- `npx backseat-ai …`: from anywhere, reads no project. `init`, `report`, `output <actorId>`, `doctor`.
- `node cli.ts …`: in your project, a person's commands. `lint`, `stately`.
- `node cli.ts --drive …`: the agent's tool. `create <machine>`, `send <actorId> <event> [payload | -]`, `snapshot <actorId>`, `describe <actorId> [<event>]`.

## Docs

- [Documentation index](https://github.com/pottedmeat/backseat-ai/blob/trunk/docs/README.md): the nine docs, in reading order.
- [XState](https://github.com/pottedmeat/backseat-ai/blob/trunk/docs/xstate.md): the XState concepts a machine is written in, and what Backseat refuses or narrows.
- [Quickstart](https://github.com/pottedmeat/backseat-ai/blob/trunk/docs/quickstart.md): setting a project up with `init`, and driving a first machine.
- [Machines](https://github.com/pottedmeat/backseat-ai/blob/trunk/docs/machines.md): writing a machine, and the keys Backseat adds.
- [CLI](https://github.com/pottedmeat/backseat-ai/blob/trunk/docs/cli.md): every command and flag.

## Optional

- [Subagents](https://github.com/pottedmeat/backseat-ai/blob/trunk/docs/subagents.md): a machine that hands work to subagents and collects what they return.
- [Driving](https://github.com/pottedmeat/backseat-ai/blob/trunk/docs/driving.md): every response a driver sees, how a refusal reads, and the exit codes.
- [Runs](https://github.com/pottedmeat/backseat-ai/blob/trunk/docs/runs.md): where a run lives, what each file in it holds, and the commands that read it.
